QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_35

question.text: Which document must disclose the fee structure (management fee, incentive fee, hurdle, catch-up) of an AIF to prospective investors?

explanation.text: The Logic: The Private Placement Memorandum is the prescribed investor disclosure document for an AIF and contains the material disclosures relating to the scheme, including proposed fees, expenses, hurdle/preferred return, carried interest and the expense structure, together with the distribution waterfall and a separate illustration of fees and expenses. The Trap: Options A and B are internal/bilateral documents; the Trust Deed and Investment Management Agreement do not serve as the investor disclosure document. Option C is irrelevant because AMFI governs mutual funds, not AIFs. Note: Source pages 149-150, 346 and 350-351 set out the PPM as the investor disclosure document and the required fee, expense, hurdle, carried-interest and waterfall disclosures.
